title: Keep Done CI comparisons refreshable while landed evidence is pending

intentCoverage.report:
Caught.

Story: SEED-288#refresh-pending-landed-evidence, revision 3322a6fd868fa8c89dfe028d33d4a935cdf741fd; .planning/seeds/SEED-288-landed-ci-evidence-follow-ups.md#refresh-pending-landed-evidence.
Promise: Check again recovers Landed in the same dashboard process when previously unanswered equivalent proof becomes available; pending evidence must not become a permanently remembered negative answer.

Fault: in dashboard/server/intentCiComparisonRead.ts, remove only the done.landedPending guard and always call rememberCiComparisonAnswer. Fixtures and assertions were unchanged in an isolated detached scratch checkout of the selected revision.
Existing protection: dashboard/tests/intent/intent-ci-comparison-pending-proof.spec.ts, “Check again recovers an unanswered equivalent proof from Branch fallback to Landed with the same source, then reuses the final answer”, assertion at line 40. The real provider fixture answers the proof after first showing Branch fallback; actual Check again then must display “Baseline compared with Landed”.

Baseline passed. With the fault, the intended assertion failed: expected “Baseline compared with Landed”, received “Baseline compared with Branch”; the preceding actual Check again at line 39 ran after the provider was made answerable. This observes the wrong behavior on the intended recovery path. Six pending-proof backend cases were also selected because Playwright path matching includes backend-tests; the exact same seven-test command was retained for baseline, fault and restoration. Fault run: six failed, one passed. Baseline and restored runs: seven passed each, no retries.
Command: caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- tests/intent/intent-ci-comparison-pending-proof.spec.ts --workers=1

Restoration: original source bytes restored, scratch Git status matched its recorded empty pre-state, and the restored command passed. The owned scratch checkout was then removed safely. Original execution checkout was never edited by the probe. Evidence: /tmp/seed288-intent-probe-result.json; /tmp/seed288-intent-{baseline,fault,restored}-proof.json and matching logs. Initial orchestration expected one selected test and stopped after the passing seven-test baseline; continuation reused that adequate baseline rather than rerunning it or resetting the invocation start.

Costs:
- Test runtime: measured sums of runner-reported attempt duration: baseline 37.294 s; fault 31.382 s; restored 37.556 s. Measured full command wall times including startup: 41.970 s, 34.416 s, 39.018 s respectively.
- Human effort: unavailable; no separate human timing record. No additional developer interaction was requested for this check.
- Agent effort: unavailable; no separate host token/active-effort measurement is exposed. Invocation elapsed is not treated as agent effort.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 264698 ms (measured), from 1794251970551 to 1794252235249 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
